lines.say: Both processes are chains of redox reactions.
OIL RIG. Oxidation is loss of electrons, reduction is gain.
Electron carriers shuttle between stages. NAD plus is reduced to NADH.
In respiration, glucose is oxidised to C O 2, and oxygen is reduced to water.
Glycolysis in the cytosol splits glucose into two pyruvate. No oxygen needed.
The link reaction removes a C O 2 and makes acetyl Co A, in the matrix.
The citric acid cycle turns twice per glucose. All the carbons leave as C O 2.
Most of the energy is now held in NADH and FADH 2.
No oxygen? Fermentation recycles NAD plus, giving only 2 ATP.

frames.heading: The pump and the water wheel

lines.say: NADH gives electrons to complex one. FADH 2 gives them to complex two.
Complexes one, three and four pump protons into the intermembrane space.

draw.alt: Proton pumps push H+ into intermembrane space; ATP synthase lets them back

lines.say: Oxygen is the final electron acceptor. It forms water at complex four.
Protons flow back through ATP synthase. Its rotor spins and makes ATP.

draw.alt: H+ flowing back through ATP synthase makes ATP

lines.say: An uncoupler is a hole in the dam. Oxygen is used, but energy becomes heat.
Each NADH gives about 2.5 ATP. Each FADH 2 gives about 1.5.
Four ATP made directly, plus 10 NADH times 2.5, plus 2 FADH 2 times 1.5.

draw.alt: ATP receipt: 4 direct, 25 from NADH, 3 from FADH2

lines.say: Glycolysis NADH may only give 1.5 each. So we say about 30 to 32.
Photosynthesis happens in the chloroplast, in two linked stages.
Light hits photosystem two, P 680. It replaces its electron by splitting water.
So the oxygen from plants comes from water, not from C O 2.
Two before one. Electrons go from photosystem two to photosystem one, then to NADPH.

draw.alt: Electron flow from PSII to PSI to NADPH

lines.say: Protons build up in the thylakoid lumen and flow out through ATP synthase.
In the stroma, rubisco attaches C O 2 to RuBP.
The product splits into two 3 P G A, which are reduced to G 3 P.
Remember 3, 6, 1, 5, 9, 6.
3 C O 2 make 6 G 3 P. One leaves, five rebuild RuBP.

draw.alt: Six G3P: one leaves, five rebuild RuBP

lines.say: That costs 9 ATP and 6 NADPH. Double it for one glucose.
The E T C doesn't make ATP. It pumps protons. ATP synthase makes the ATP.
Mitochondria pump into the intermembrane space. Chloroplasts pump into the thylakoid lumen.
The Calvin cycle still depends on ATP and NADPH from the light reactions.
Oxygen is only used at complex four, as the final electron acceptor.
